turns.doctor_question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, doctor. It’s very nice to meet you, too. Thank you for seeing me. 

Um, I’m here because... well, I hope I don't sound difficult or anything, but for a few months now, I’ve just been noticing this... pattern. I supervise an administrative office, so I'm very used to keeping track of details, you know? And lately, my sister’s appointments keep getting moved without me knowing, and her bills are showing up wrong, and people just conveniently "forget" to call me back. 

Everyone keeps telling me it’s just innocent clerical mistakes, and I really try to be understanding, I do. But... I just know they’re keeping information from me. It really feels like they're working together to push me out of the decisions regarding her. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a fixed belief that people are intentionally keeping information from them and conspiring to push them out of decisions, despite being told they are just clerical mistakes.

turns.doctor_question: If someone showed you clear proof that these scheduling and billing problems were simple mistakes, would you be able to accept that?
turns.patient_response:
Well... I really, really wish I could. I know it would make everything so much easier for everyone, and I hate being the person who causes a fuss. I really try to be agreeable. 

But... even if someone showed me what looked like proof... I just couldn't accept it. I know that probably sounds stubborn, and I'm so sorry, I don't mean to be difficult at all. It's just that I've been seeing this pattern for months. The moved appointments, the incorrect bills, the unreturned calls... it's all too consistent. Even when everyone insists it's just a series of innocent mistakes, I just... I know in my heart they're keeping information from me. I know they're working together to push me out of the decisions regarding my sister. 

I hope you're not upset with me for saying that. I know it's not what people usually want to hear, but I promised to be completely honest with you. Am I doing okay? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions the right way.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been diagnosed with any neurological or other medical illness that you think might be related to these experiences?

Oh, goodness, no. No, I haven't. I'm actually very healthy, thankfully. I've always made a point to stay on top of my annual physicals and everything, especially since I spend so much time at a desk managing the office. You really have to take care of yourself, you know? 

But no, I don't have any neurological conditions or... or any medical illnesses like that at all. My regular doctor says I'm doing really well for fifty-nine. So there's definitely no medical issue that would be confusing my thinking or causing me to imagine things, if that's what you mean. 

I hope that's a good thing? I mean, I just want to reassure you that my mind and my body are completely fine. Does that help rule things out for your notes? I want to be as helpful as I can.

turns.doctor_question: Before the issues with your sister began, have you generally tended to mistrust other people and suspect that they might take advantage of you?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, no, definitely not! I've always prided myself on being a very trusting person, actually. I really try to see the best in everyone. 

In my line of work—managing the office—you have to be able to trust your team, and I've always had wonderful relationships with my coworkers and friends. I'm usually the one organizing the office potlucks and making sure everyone feels included. I would never just assume someone was out to get me or take advantage. That's just not who I am at all. 

That's why this whole situation with the clinic has been so upsetting for me. It's completely out of the ordinary for me to feel this way about people. I really wish I didn't have to be so suspicious of them, but... well, they've just given me no choice, with how they're acting. 

But generally speaking? Oh, no, I'm very trusting. I hope that doesn't make me sound naive! I just prefer to be positive. Is that the kind of information you were looking for? I want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture of what I'm usually like.
